lines.japanese: にこにこアルバイター千歳の、色んなひととお話しちゃうぞシリーズ！
lines.english: Smiling Part-Timer Chitose Presents: Conversations with All Kinds of People!

lines.japanese: 「ぬるっと行こう！」
lines.english: “Let's keep it slippery!”

lines.japanese: さてさて、今日も男性スタッフ最後のお勤め、クローズ作業に入っております。
lines.english: Now, then. Once again, we'd reached the last duty of the day for the male staff: closing.

lines.japanese: 出だしも肝心ですが、明日に繋げる一日の締め、これもまた同じくらい大切なことだと思うんですよね。
lines.english: A good beginning matters, but the way you close one day and carry it into tomorrow matters just as much. Don't you think?

lines.japanese: そして、労働を通した様々な自我とのコミュニケーション。これってお仕事をしている上で、面白い部分のひとつだと思いません？
lines.english: And all the different personalities you get to know through work—isn't that one of the fun parts of having a job?

lines.japanese: 「千歳君、その洗い物は俺がやるからいいよ」
lines.english: “Chitose, I'll take care of those dishes.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、すいません。じゃあ俺、フロア清掃戻りまっす」
lines.english: “Oh, thanks. Then I'll get back to the floor.”

lines.japanese: 俺がシンクで食器や調理具の洗浄作業をしていると、服飾の専門学校に通っているというおしゃれな三澤さんがやってきました。
lines.english: I was at the sink washing dishes and kitchen utensils when Misawa came over—a stylish fellow who, I had heard, attended fashion school.

lines.japanese: 三澤さんは、えーそうですねー、一言で評すならお喋りさん……というか、語りたがりさんです。
lines.english: How to describe Misawa? In a word, he was talkative... Or rather, a man who liked to hold forth.

lines.japanese: ご自覚はないのかもしれませんが、とにかくよく語っておられます。黙って聞いていると、取り留めのないことを延々語りつづけます。
lines.english: He might not realize it, but the man certainly loved to talk. If you just listened quietly, he'd ramble on forever about nothing in particular.

lines.japanese: こういう方に対しては、こちらは聞き手に徹し、たまに促し程度の相槌を打つだけで良いので気が楽です。
lines.english: With someone like him, all I had to do was listen and offer the occasional encouraging murmur. Easy work.

lines.japanese: 「千歳君はもう冬休みの予定とか決まってるの？　俺は学校の連中とスノボでもやろうかって計画立ててるんだけど」
lines.english: “Know what you're doing for winter break yet, Chitose? Some people from school and I are thinking of going snowboarding.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。自分あんま冬休みとか関係ないすけど、さすが三澤さんは趣味もおしゃれっすね」
lines.english: “Right. Winter break doesn't mean much to me, but even your hobbies are stylish, Misawa.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　べつに普通だって。千歳君だってスキーとかスノボぐらいやるでしょ」
lines.english: “What? That's completely ordinary. You must ski or snowboard sometimes too, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。あまりやんないすけど、服飾学校のみなさんはウェアからしておしゃれそっすね」
lines.english: “Right. Not often, but I bet everyone at fashion school even has stylish snow gear.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、そんなことないよ。俺だって、なんだかんだ言って、こういう店でアルバイトしちゃってるわけだしさ」
lines.english: “Ha ha, hardly. I mean, one way or another, I've wound up working part-time in a place like this.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。アレキサンダー、こういう店っすね」
lines.english: “Right. Alexander certainly is a place like this.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ条件さえ合うなら、もっと個人経営のカフェとかね、制服じゃなくて私服でやるような、そういうお店でバイトしたいと思うけどさ」
lines.english: “If the conditions were right, sure, I'd rather work at some independent café. You know, the sort of place where you wear your own clothes instead of a uniform.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。アレキサンダー、チェーン店っすもんね」
lines.english: “Right. Alexander is a chain, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、こういう店だと、環境音にしても本部からの指示通りに流さなくちゃいけないでしょ。俺はファッションやムーブメントって、キホン音楽から作られると思ってるひとだから、正直きびしいんだよね」
lines.english: “Exactly. In a place like this, even the background music has to follow orders from headquarters. I'm the sort of person who believes music is where fashion and every new cultural movement begin, so honestly, it's stifling.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。アレキサンダー、ポップス中心っすもんね」
lines.english: “Right. Alexander mostly plays pop.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、一応ビルボード２０位らへんの曲とか、アングラシーンの中でのアンセムとか？　キャッチーでありながらミーハーになり過ぎずって風に、頭使ってるのは分かるんだけどね。どうも足りてないっていうか」
lines.english: “I can tell they've put some thought into it, I suppose. Songs hovering around number twenty on Billboard, anthems from the underground scene, that sort of thing. Catchy without going too mainstream. But somehow it still falls short.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。でも誰もが納得いくようには出来ないっすもんね」
lines.english: “Right. Though you can't please everyone.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そういう問題じゃなくてさ。たとえばユニフォームにしたって、あのメイド服みたいなさ、日本じゃ萌えっていうの？　一部で流行っちゃ流行なんだろうけど、それはどうなの？　って思うよね」
lines.english: “No, that isn’t the issue. Take the uniforms. They’re practically maid costumes—what do people here in Japan call that, the whole cutesy craze? I suppose it’s fashionable in certain circles, but you’ve got to wonder.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。でも制服目当てのお客さんもいらっしゃいますしね」
lines.english: “Right. Though some customers do come for the uniforms.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、そうやって、自らのステータスを下げてるんだよこの店は。俺はね、２１世紀はもう店が客を選ぶ時代だと思うんだ。いま欧米で認められてるカフェは、みんなその辺よく分かってるよ。大したものだろう？」
lines.english: “Exactly. This place lowers its own status. I think the twenty-first century is the age when establishments choose their customers. Every respected café in Europe and America understands that. Impressive, wouldn't you say?”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。じゃ三澤さんは将来そういうおしゃれなカフェで働きたいわけっすね」
lines.english: “Right. So in the future, you want to work at one of those fashionable cafés.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？　俺デザイナー志望だよ」
lines.english: “Why would I? I'm going to be a designer.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。きっと立派なデザイナーになるっすね」
lines.english: “Right. I'm sure you'll make an excellent one.”

lines.japanese: 三澤さんは世のひとびとをナチュラルに見下していらっしゃいますが、意外と身内には優しく、たっぷりと色んな話を聞かせてくださいます。そのせいで作業が遅れがちなことは難点ですが。
lines.english: Misawa looked down on humanity as naturally as breathing, yet was surprisingly kind to people in his circle, generously sharing one thought after another. The drawback was that the work tended to fall behind while he did it.

lines.japanese: 今日のクローズ作業が終わった時間は、いつもよりやや遅めの１０時３０分ほどでした。
lines.english: We finished closing at around ten thirty that night, a little later than usual.

lines.japanese: あーあ、予想以上に遅くなっちゃった。
lines.english: Oh, man. That had taken longer than I expected.

lines.japanese: やや急ぎ足で階段を上り、『ＳＴＡＦＦ　ＯＮＬＹ』と打ち込んである扉の前に駆けよりました
lines.english: I hurried up the stairs toward the door stamped STAFF ONLY.

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、こんな時間っ！」
lines.english: “Damn it, look at the time!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、もうこんな時間……」
lines.english: “Oh... Look at the time...”

lines.japanese: 二人分の力が加わったドアは、ほとんど重さを感じずに開きました。
lines.english: The door flew open under the force of both our hands, as if it weighed nothing at all.

lines.japanese: その状況を整理するのに、お互い十数秒。ああ、内と外とで同時にドアを開けたのか。
lines.english: It took us both a good ten seconds to make sense of the situation. Ah. We had opened the same door from opposite sides at the exact same time.

lines.japanese: 「おっ、お疲れさまです！」
lines.english: “O-oh. Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、お疲れさまです」
lines.english: “Hi.”

lines.japanese: 「えと……何してたんですか？」
lines.english: “Um... What were you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　何とは？」
lines.english: “What? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「ああいえ、いままでクローズ作業なさってたんですか？」
lines.english: “Oh, no—I mean, were you closing all this time?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、それが今日は三澤さんと一緒で……」
lines.english: “Yes. I was with Misawa tonight, and...”

lines.japanese: 彼女は「ああ」という表情をして、口をつぐみました。
lines.english: Her face said, *Ah, that explains it,* and she fell silent.

lines.japanese: なぜかアレキサンダーのスタッフは男女とも喋りたがり屋さんが多いですが、日和子さんだけは安心して会話の間を取ってくれるなあ。
lines.english: For some reason, Alexander had no shortage of compulsive talkers, men or women. Hiyoko alone could be trusted to let a silence breathe.

lines.japanese: 単純に、あまり俺と話したくないだけかもしれませんが。
lines.english: Though maybe she simply didn't want to talk to me very much.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さんはいまから帰るところですか」
lines.english: “Are you heading home now, Hiyoko?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そりゃ分かりますよ。だって、ここから出るってことは帰るってことでしょ？」
lines.english: “Well, I can tell that much. Coming out of here means you're going home, right?”

lines.japanese: ん？　しかしよく見ると、彼女の手にはいつものバッグが握られてません。
lines.english: Hm? On closer inspection, though, her usual bag wasn't in her hand.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、まあ……」
lines.english: “Yes, well...”

lines.japanese: でも肯定してるんだから帰るところで間違いないのでしょう。俺が余計な詮索をすることじゃありません。
lines.english: Still, she had said yes, so I must have been right about her going home. It wasn't my place to pry.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ＣＤ」
lines.english: “Oh, the CD.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「さっき話してたＣＤ、見せてください」
lines.english: “Could you show me the CD we were talking about earlier?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、はいはい」
lines.english: “Ah. Of course.”

lines.japanese: そういえばしましたね、そんな約束。
lines.english: Oh, right. I'd promised her that.

lines.japanese: あれ……もしかして日和子さん、そのために俺を待ってたとか……？
lines.english: Wait... Could Hiyoko have been waiting for me... just for that?

lines.japanese: ロッカーの鞄からフリッキー５の復刻版ベストアルバムを取りだして彼女に渡しました。
lines.english: I took the reissued Fricky Five greatest-hits album from the bag in my locker and handed it to her.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり細川君ってかっこいいよねー」
lines.english: “Hosokawa really is handsome, isn't he?”

lines.japanese: アルバムを手にした途端、日和子さんは年齢相応の笑顔を浮かべました。
lines.english: The instant the album reached her hands, Hiyoko smiled like any other girl her age.

lines.japanese: 「うわ、なんすかその満面の笑みは」
lines.english: “Whoa. What's with the ear-to-ear grin?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いいじゃないですか、ちょっとくらいほころんだって！」
lines.english: “W-what's wrong with smiling a little!?”

lines.japanese: 「いやそれ、ほころんでるなんて可愛いものじゃないですよ。にやけてるって言うんですよ」
lines.english: “That's way past a little smile. You're grinning like an idiot.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ひどい！」
lines.english: “Oh, that's mean!”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんがＣＤを胸に抱いて抗議してきました。いや、抗議というよりも、まるでじゃれるような……うーん、ほほえましいなあ。
lines.english: Hiyoko hugged the CD to her chest and protested. No, it was less a protest than playful banter... Hmm. How sweet.

lines.japanese: って、いかんいかん。せっかくの日和子さんとの御歓談だけど、今日はこのあと祥玄社さんへ行くアポがあるのです。
lines.english: Wait, no, no. Much as I was enjoying this delightful chat with Hiyoko, I had an appointment at Shogensha afterward.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃあ俺、着替えてきますね」
lines.english: “Well, I'm going to change.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Ah. Yes.”

lines.japanese: これにてさよなら、かと思いきや──
lines.english: I thought that would be goodbye—

lines.japanese: ──しかし日和子さんは退室せず、その手にＣＤを持ったまま、すっぽりソファーへ座りこんでしまいました。
lines.english: —but Hiyoko didn't leave. Still holding the CD, she settled deep into the sofa.

lines.japanese: あれ？　なんで帰らない？　そのアルバムを貸してくれという意思表示？　それとも何か他に聞きたいことでも？
lines.english: Huh? Why wasn't she going home? Was this her way of asking to borrow the album? Or was there something else she wanted to ask?

lines.japanese: なんて考えもしましたが、とにかく時間がないので、俺はさっさと着替えを済ませることにしました。
lines.english: The possibilities crossed my mind, but I was out of time, so I hurried off to change.

lines.japanese: やっぱり日和子さん、フリファのＣＤが目的で待ってた……みたいだな。
lines.english: So Hiyoko really had waited here... for the Frickies CD.

lines.japanese: いやいや、だって、そうじゃなかったらなんでこんな時間までひとりで残ってた？
lines.english: No, of course she had. Why else would she stay here alone this late?

lines.japanese: 千歳君と一緒に帰りたくて？　ははは、そんなおめでたい話があるわきゃない。
lines.english: Because she'd wanted to walk home with little old me? Ha ha ha. As if anything that convenient could happen.

lines.japanese: 帰りの支度を整えて扉を開けると、復刻版のアルバムを眺めていた日和子さんがこっちを見上げました。
lines.english: Ready to leave, I opened the door. Hiyoko looked up from the reissued album she had been studying.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、どうも」
lines.english: “Oh. Hi.”

lines.japanese: 「どもっす、お待たせしちゃってすいません」
lines.english: “Hey. Sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: べつに俺を待ってたわけじゃないだろ。なに言ってんだ俺。
lines.english: She hadn't been waiting for me. What was I talking about?

lines.japanese: でも日和子さんからの否定もありません。うーん、なんていうか。
lines.english: But Hiyoko didn't deny it either. Hmm. How could I put this?

lines.japanese: 例えばこう、ギャグを言うときに「あ、いまの俺なに言っても面白いな」っていう空気ありますよね。なんかいまが正にそんな感じ。
lines.english: You know that mood when you make a joke and think, *Oh, anything I say right now will land*? That was exactly what the air felt like.

lines.japanese: このままなら日和子さんと楽しいお話なんかして、あわよくば一緒に帰ったりも出来そうな空気を感じるんですが。
lines.english: In that mood, it felt as if I could keep chatting with Hiyoko and, with any luck, even walk home with her.

lines.japanese: ですが。
lines.english: But.

lines.japanese: 「それ、良かったらお貸ししますよ」
lines.english: “You can borrow that, if you'd like.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、これ？　あ、いいんですか？」
lines.english: “What? Oh, this? A-are you sure?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、今日は自分、編集部の方に顔を出さないといけないんで。どうぞ持って帰っちゃってください。あ、返却はいつでもいっすよ」
lines.english: “Of course. I have to stop by the editorial office tonight, so go ahead and take it home. Return it whenever you like.”

lines.japanese: 「編集部？　今からですか？」
lines.english: “The editorial office? Now?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 今日はお仕事の話。しかも俺の方から頼みこんだ用事なので、米田さんを待たせるわけにはいきません。
lines.english: Tonight's appointment was business, and I was the one who had asked for it. I couldn't keep Yoneda waiting.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんもよく言ってるように、公私のけじめはつけないとね。たとえいまが数少ないチャンスのひとつだったとしても。
lines.english: As Hiyoko was always saying, one had to keep business and personal matters separate. Even if this was one of the precious few chances I ever got.

lines.japanese: 「そうですか……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんには、ライターとしての仕事もありますもんね」
lines.english: “You have your writing work too, Mr. Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 場を繋ぐための言葉とは違う、湿った重みがありました。
lines.english: The words hung damp and heavy between us, nothing like idle speech meant merely to fill a silence.

lines.japanese: もしかして、俺が曲がりなりにも物書きとしての仕事をしてることに、先達として疎外感でも感じてしまったのでしょうか。
lines.english: Maybe the fact that even I had found paid work as a writer made her, the senior writer, feel somehow left out.

lines.japanese: そんなことを思いながらも、俺はスポーツバッグの中から大判の封筒をちらりと覗かせました。
lines.english: Even as I wondered, I let the large envelope inside my sports bag show just enough for her to see.

lines.japanese: 「これ、例の書評なんですよ」
lines.english: “This is the review I mentioned.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「完成したんですぐにでも届けたくて」
lines.english: “I finished it, and I wanted to deliver it right away.”

lines.japanese: 「男性誌の小さな囲み記事なんて大した宣伝効果はないんでしょうけど、でも、やっぱりひとりでも多くに細川玉木作品を知ってもらいたいじゃないすか」
lines.english: “A little sidebar in a men's magazine probably won't sell many books, but I still want as many people as possible to discover Tamaki Hosokawa's work.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんがじっと見ています。
lines.english: Hiyoko stared at me.

lines.japanese: ああ、こんな日に限ってそんな、後ろ髪を引っぱるように。
lines.english: Why did she have to look at me that way tonight of all nights, making it so hard to leave?

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そんなわけなんで、走ってかなくちゃならないんで！　じゃ！」
lines.english: “So, anyway, I've got to run! See you!”

lines.japanese: 俺はしゅびっと手を上げて階段を駆けおりました。
lines.english: I snapped off a jaunty wave and raced down the stairs.

lines.japanese: 店を出て、靴のつま先をとんとん地面で馴染ませていると、ふと二階の窓にひとの姿が見えたような気がします。
lines.english: Outside the restaurant, I tapped my toes against the pavement to settle my shoes. For an instant, I thought I saw someone at the second-floor window.

lines.japanese: さて、彼女はあんなところで何を見ているんでしょう。たったいま出ていった男の見送りでもしてくれたんでしょうか。
lines.english: What could she be looking at from up there? Had she come to see off the man who had just walked out?

lines.japanese: いや、彼女はきっと空を見ているんでしょう。願いが叶いますようにと。
lines.english: No. She was probably looking up at the sky, hoping her wish would come true.
